column1: 401541|C|The moduli space, cover and rational cohomology target are specified.|Compute all rational cohomology degrees of the bitangent cover; degree 28 alone does not determine them. Requires equivariant moduli topology; no small full-scope computation identified.

401542|C|The final uniform-entry formulation supplies the missing glyphs in the first sentence.|As n tends to infinity both partitions are uniformly sampled, not merely the degree column. Character parity asymptotics need distribution control over all conjugacy classes. Recalled public-resolution lead only; no body clearance.

401558|C|Common anisotropic-system convention specifies simultaneous nonzero zeros; field and r are universal.|Every p-adic K and r>=1: equality u_r=4r. Diagonal examples provide lower bounds only; upper bounds require uniform common-zero theory. No bounded full-scope route.

401565|D|Good characteristic and genus equivalence are not defined; G must be interpreted over K.|Finiteness for every finitely generated K and absolutely simple simply connected K-group is not a finite enumeration problem. Need the exact good-characteristic exclusions and maximal-torus genus definition first.

401566|D|F, cohomological coefficients and BG/unramified conventions are omitted.|Triviality for all mixed Dynkin types cannot be inferred by treating each simple factor separately; central quotients may mix factors. No source-defined invariant or uniform bridge checked.

401573|C|All fields, extensions, objects, vanishing equivalence and density requirement are stated.|One finite-type smooth geometrically integral X must work for every l/k, with both equivalence directions and density. Existing ind-variety approximation does not give a uniform finite stage. No route to that compactness step.

401579|C|Free group rank and property (T) have standard meanings and rank range is explicit.|All d>=5; a proof for one rank needs a valid propagation theorem. Recollection of established property-(T) results is a prior objection, not a body-verified resolution here. HOLD without new certificate investment.

401584|D|The correlation sets C_qa and C_qc are not defined in the literal.|All n,k equality is a universal operator-algebra assertion. Recalled nonlocal-game separation is a strong prior lead; definitions and actual separation theorem body remain unread. No novelty claim.

401591|C|State, countable projection additivity and sequential weak-star continuity are standard and quantified.|Every von Neumann algebra, state and weak-star convergent sequence; normality cannot simply be substituted for countable additivity in arbitrary algebras. Set-theoretic and nonseparable issues block a routine sequential argument.

401593|S|State space and finiteness of entropy terms are unspecified; infinity-minus-infinity may occur.|For every positive A, a weighted variation bound is stronger than trace-norm Pinsker alone. Need finite entropy or a defined relative-entropy extension and the meaning of absolute functional variation before proving it.

401614|C|Uniform labelled planar graph model, core and high-probability limit are explicit.|Need a positive linear-size connected component within the 3-core, not merely linear total core size. Enumeration of planar graphs and concentration plus connectivity are substantial dependencies.

401622|C|The full Witt algebra, bracket, base field and ideal quantifier are explicit despite stray glyphs.|Every nonzero two-sided ideal, including nonhomogeneous ones, must yield finite GK dimension. Finite presentations or low-degree ideal tests cannot resolve this universal ideal statement.

401625|C|Chebotarev count, Galois data, every fixed positive epsilon and asymptotic are explicit.|Already E=Q asks prime asymptotics on every x^epsilon interval. This is a deep short-interval obstruction; finite prime counts and GRH-sized intervals do not give the requested quantifier.

401635|C|Undecidable and finite extension are standard field-theoretic notions.|Every finite extension of an undecidable field: undecidability need not transfer just from inclusion because the base field may not be definable. Need a full definability or interpretation mechanism.

401636|C|Decidability is explicitly first-order ring-theory decidability.|Every finite extension L/K of every decidable K; an algebraic presentation with coefficients requires effective access to their types, not just decidability of parameter-free Th(K). No uniform transfer proof supplied.

401639|S|Solvable may mean weak or proper solution, which changes the assertion materially.|Every large K and finite split embedding problem over K(x); weak solutions follow from splitting and would be routine. Proper solutions require Galois realization and a genuine geometric argument. Source scope needed.

401672|C|Genus, boundary count, metric class and supremum are specified using standard Steklov notation.|For each k>=1 a smooth maximizer must attain the supremum. Compactness can develop bubbles or degenerations; checking the disk or annulus does not establish all k. No short universal existence route.

401689|C|Dimension, smoothness, rationality, affineness and infinitude of real forms are explicit.|Every d>=4 requires infinitely many pairwise inequivalent real structures. Products can propagate dimension only after a genuine base example and nonisomorphism invariant; neither constructed here.

401691|D|Rational smooth embedding and non-rectifiability require the source birational convention.|For each d>=5 the nodal rational projective closure must also give a real smooth embedded affine line and fail rectifiability. Merely drawing a degree-d nodal curve does not meet the real/birational conditions.

401713|C|The cover and resolvent-degree target are specified; standard RD applies.|Equality RD=3 requires both upper and lower bounds. Classical line formulas or a low-parameter auxiliary cover yield only one direction; a lower-bound obstruction is not supplied.

401738|D|The coexact spectral quantity and precise metric/certification convention are left to Theorem 2.|A fixed numerical enclosure is explicitly attributed to a theorem, so reproducing it is not discovery. Rigorous spectral truncation/tail control would be needed even for certification; theorem body not read.

401748|S|The group class, topology and coefficient continuity conventions are omitted.|All coefficient algebras is materially stronger than coefficient-free Baum-Connes. Recalled counterexamples are a strong prior objection, not verified here. Arbitrary wording supplies no new credit route.

401751|D|R(V,K) and W_q(V,K) are undefined and the statement refers to setup above.|Need an actual K with exactly one side of the resonance/vanishing equivalence true in small positive characteristic. Computing an unnamed Koszul module without the source conventions risks a different problem.

401756|S|Base field/characteristic and geometric category of the ppav are unspecified.|Every point of every indecomposable g-dimensional ppav must satisfy the half-dimension multiplicity bound. Generic or Jacobian examples cannot certify the universal class. Scope and deep singularity theory remain.

401758|C|For finite matroids the rank-flat counts and all k<=d/2 give the full standard target.|All matroids and all lower-half ranks; counting special representable families cannot resolve it. Strong recollection of an existing top-heavy theorem defeats investment pending actual primary body confirmation; no theorem-body clearance claimed.

401761|D|Special subvariety is not defined and holomorphic-symplectic assumptions need the source category.|All codimensions 0..n for all X; existence of arbitrary subvarieties does not imply the source special/isotropic property. No precise construction target available from the literal alone.

401764|C|Surface, unramified Brauer class, real evaluation condition and index/period equality are specified.|Every such surface and class; vanishing real evaluations removes a real obstruction but does not itself construct a splitting field of degree period. Likely theorem-like source lead, body unread; no short new bridge.

401815|C|Both hulls and the entire bounded continuous PSH test class are defined.|For every M,w0,w, domination of all test functions must force equality for every test function. One cannot negate a PSH function; convex increasing composition alone does not reverse the ordering. No full mechanism survives that obstruction.

401817|D|Finite surface, second kind, irreducibility and the (g,m)-bundle equivalence need definitions.|Finiteness up to isotopy must hold for all allowed bases. Noncompact base and reducible monodromy examples need exclusion checks, so no ordinary compact-moduli finiteness shortcut is justified.

401831|I|Models [6], [10], [11], equations and requested extension properties are absent.|No literal PDE, boundary data or well-posedness criterion is available. Retain missing-scope row; neither an ODE toy model nor an invented PDE is a replacement.

401837|D|Loop weights, alpha convention and meaning of KT transition are not defined.|All 0<n<=2: locating a proposed threshold is weaker than proving KT behavior. Integrability or critical weights alone do not control essential singularity and phase behavior for the whole range.

401840|D|The constants a_i,j and their required values/nonzero status are unspecified.|All nine height pairs need exact logarithmic covariance asymptotics under the infinite-volume measure. Height-one calculations do not establish higher-height correlations; no finite certificate or uniform analytic route.

401842|I|Neither the Lipschitz construction nor a precise percolation model or success property is stated.|A general applicability comment is not a quantified theorem. No replacement model chosen; full source definitions would be necessary before evaluating a route.

401877|C|Curve genus, generality, series locus and multiplication map are explicit.|For a general C, every L in W^6_26 must work; proving a single L or dimension-count heuristic is insufficient. Source may implicitly mean complete linear series. Requires a uniform degeneracy-locus argument.

401885|D|Volume normalization, compactification, tautological xi and psi conventions are not defined.|All admissible g,n,mu; an intersection formula is sensitive to area normalization and stack multiplicities. Small-stratum calculations do not prove the universal identity; no short route or prior-body audit.

401890|D|The strong-game length L(K_t,n), winning conventions and length optimization are undefined.|For each t one bound must be independent of board size n. Ramsey existence alone gives a board-size-dependent strategy; no constant-move forcing construction produced.

401897|C|Symbolic powers, ordinary powers, complex point ideals and all m are standard and explicit.|All finite point sets and m>=1. Recalled classical containment counterexamples make this a high-priority prior objection, not a new hypothesis; no primary counterexample body inspected here. No credit for rediscovery.

401898|D|The malformed hat-alpha symbol is not defined and base field is absent.|For every m the bound concerns the asymptotic initial degree, not merely alpha(I). Differentiation bounds or finitely many m do not establish the displayed full inequality. Need primary definitions and field first.

401902|S|Regular-ring hypotheses and symbolic-power conventions for general rings are not restricted.|For every radical I there must be an ideal-dependent threshold N after which all n work. A counterexample to an early n or a threshold for points alone does not settle stable universal containment.

401907|C|The fixed dimension, optimal coherence value and complete Gram matrix are supplied.|Exact executed check: A has characteristic polynomial (t-2)(t^2+t-3)^2, and I+mu A has rank 3. This verifies the already printed construction, not global optimality. Welch only gives sqrt(1/6)<mu; matching lower bound remains substantial. PARK, no proposal.

401909|S|Endpoint constraints on n,d and nontrivial frame conventions are absent; terminal text contains corruption.|The disjunction must hold for every existing complex ETF, not every integer pair passing Welch. Arithmetic searches over parameters cannot construct a violating ETF. Endpoint divisibility conventions must be fixed first.

401910|S|Every d includes d=1 where ambient dimension 4d-5 is negative.|Meaningful d>=2 still requires Haar-probability control and a limit as d grows. Removing the invalid endpoint is only wording repair, not a new counterexample; no geometric probability proof provided.

401913|S|No distinctness or spanning/tightness is required, so alpha=1 repeated vectors satisfy the literal.|For each d take all d^2 vectors equal to e1 and alpha=1. This is a domain/wording defect, earns no credit, and says nothing about the intended maximal equiangular lines/SIC existence problem.

401920|D|Optimal-insulation functional, eigenproblem, mass convention and dimension are missing.|For every sufficiently small m every optimizer must break symmetry and have positive-measure gaps. A nonradial competitor alone does not establish these two universal claims. No variational route without the source problem.

401922|D|Soft theta function, measure class, z, rescaling and uniqueness equivalence are undefined.|Every alpha and all periodic unit-density configurations is stronger than Bravais-lattice optimality. Translational/rotational equivalence and measure scaling must be pinned; Bravais results cannot silently cover unions.

401944|C|Simple regular graph, proper k-edge-colouring and rainbow path length are explicit.|For every k>=3 all such graphs must admit k-1 distinct-colour edges in a simple path. Greedy extension only forces roughly half the degree because used colours and used vertices each block edges. No rotation-extension argument closing the full bound found.

401953|S|For epsilon>=1/2 the promise sides overlap; intended small-epsilon range is implicit.|For each small epsilon a finite alphabet k and an NP-hardness reduction are needed. This is theorem-like 2-to-1 Games content with a strong known-result objection; no primary reduction body read or new proof proposed.

401955|S|Approximation convention, randomness, computational model and alphabet scaling are unspecified.|A single positive exponent improvement for 1.1 approximation must work on all inputs in the intended alphabet regime. Existing coarse approximations and special-alphabet algorithms are not full-scope bridges.

401961|D|P-hat, tilde-A, G_1T and fundamental-box conventions are source dependent.|All prime characteristics and all indicated alcoves require actual tilting/projective-module identifications. Known small-characteristic counterexample leads need exact weight matching and source bodies; no new credit candidate.

401967|D|The quantum affine algebra type, monomial order and polynomial construction are unspecified.|All comparable monomials need both Grothendieck multiplicities and polynomial positivity. Computing a few modules cannot prove the universal character formula; no source-defined full route.
